title: common-dir lock: reset a waiter deadline when the holder changes (DEC-282 (a9) item 2)
description: Follow-up, NOT a 0.15.1 gate and no dependency on the 0.15.1 release task (QCLI-577). opum-doc DEC-282 (a9) item 2 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1865, under ODOC-610), verbatim: "opum-doc addition: the queue case does not vanish entirely. Waiters whose inputs DIFFER (refs moving between runs) cannot reuse, and still serialise. Two things keep that case bounded in 0.15.1. Q563 per-ref cache makes each such run re-read only the changed refs, so the runs are short. And an expiry there is not silent, because of (a8) item 2 stderr line. The exact fix is a follow-up, not a 0.15.1 gate: a waiter deadline resets whenever the holder CHANGES (progress observed), so it expires only against one holder that has held too long, which is (a8) premise again. It is filed in both quest-cli and lore-cli for the patch after 0.15.1, beside QCLI-571, so the pair stays consistent ((a8) item 3)." Target: the patch after 0.15.1 (QCLI-575, retargeted to 0.15.2), beside QCLI-571. Origin: Opus review of #767 finding 2 (expiry is reachable behind a queue of live holders). Work on it after 0.15.1, not now. lore-cli files the same follow-up for its lock.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A waiter deadline in the common-dir lock resets whenever the lock holder changes (a different owner token is observed), so it expires only against one holder that has held for longer than the wait
A test proves a waiter behind several short consecutive holders does not expire, and one against a single long-held holder does, each red with the reset removed or always applied
The unlocked-expiry stderr note of DEC-282 (a8) item 2 is unchanged, and lore-cli lock behaves the same (a8 item 3)

implementationNotes: DEC-282 (a10), opum-doc, opum-ai/opum-doc#1866 under ODOC-610 (relayed by the leader), ACCEPTS the lore/quest lock difference for 0.15.1 only: lore is ahead of the rule, not wrong; quest version only matters for a waiter whose inputs differ, under a queue, and that case is short (QCLI-563 per-ref cache) and announced (the (a8) item 2 stderr line); quest brings the pair level in this after-0.15.1 follow-up, filed beside QCLI-571. Fact for the implementation: lore-cli#746 ALREADY resets a waiter deadline when the holder owner changes (lore-cli advisory-lock.ts around :568 and :641); lore filed its twin as LCLI-806 (opum-ai/lore-cli#748). The quest twin is therefore the real implementation plus a pinning test, not only a test. Nothing changes in #767 for it. Both 0.15.1 CHANGELOGs state the difference in one line (owed on the 0.15.1 bump, QCLI-577).
